current_activity: Walcheren: 157th Brigade relieves the Canadians at the causeway and wades the Sloe Channel at 03:30 on 3 Nov
notes: Event date: 3 November 1944, 03:30 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 111, 114). Event definition: After the Canadian attacks of 31 October and 1-2 November, a battalion of the 157th Brigade relieves the Canadians at the Walcheren causeway on 2 November under cover of Typhoon rockets; at 03:30 on the 3rd the brigade outflanks the causeway by crossing the Sloe Channel in boats and wading a mile along the mud shore, without serious opposition; the 156th Brigade follows on the 4th and both brigades then link up and advance towards Middelburg (p. 114); the earlier landing on South Beveland, with the leading troops of the division crossing the Scheldt, is dated about 26 October (p. 111). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 114: "Then under cover of a heavy rocket attack by Typhoons they were relieved by a battalion of the 157th Brigade of the 52nd (Lowland) Division"; "At 3.30 on the morning of the 3rd this was done without serious opposition"; p. 111: "the 52nd Division's leading troops had crossed the Scheldt and were landing on South Beveland". Location: Sloedam (Walcheren causeway), Zeeland (existing place PL0685) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the Sloedam causeway, where the brigade crossed the channel; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names the Walcheren causeway and the Sloe Channel crossing (p. 114). Review (British Batch 2, 28 October 2026; inferred value; old value: operation_id OP-SCHELDT; new value: operation_id OP-INFATUATE): the row describes the fighting on Walcheren on 2 to 6 November 1944, the assault that Stacey, pp. 379-380 and 407, names Operation Infatuate (Infatuate I at Flushing, Infatuate II at Westkapelle; Ellis, vol. II, p. 114, dates the attack to 1 November and p. 123 the end to 8 November); the new operation is a child of OP-SCHELDT, so the narrower operation replaces the broader one. The Canadian Army row of 8 November (C1283) stays under OP-SCHELDT because it also closes the whole Scheldt battle.
